messages:
sam: FYI canary deploy (deploy-id: d-78c2) flipped batching density heuristic + enabled KV prefetch on model-xyz, p99 on canary jumped ~3x within 5m. Watching metrics now.

dmitri: copying — which heuristic change exactly? density param or microbatch cap?

ci-bot: Canary rollout started for d-78c2 -> 10% traffic routed to canary (hosts: canary-07..canary-10).

lee: @sam can you paste the p95/p99 scrape?

sam: metrics snippet:
```
canary: p50=45ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms
baseline: p50=42ms, p95=120ms, p99=130ms
error-rate ~unchanged
```

maya: whoa p99 420ms. sounds like tailing from batching density causing oversized microbatches in low-qps tails. did we change max_microbatch_size?

sam: we set density target from 0.6 -> 0.85 and relaxed microbatch upper cap from 16 -> 32 for the canary. KV prefetch toggled from off -> on for warmup.

dmitri: toggling density up can increase waiting time per-request; but 3x p99 is large. the profiling flame shows long wait in "batch_manager::await_batch_fill" and then an expensive kernel chosen for 32 length seq. pasting stack:
```
# perf summary
batch_manager::await_batch_fill  62%
kernel_selector::choose_kernel  18%  -> selected kernel: fast-gemm-uint8-32seq
kv_cache::prefetch_worker      10%  -> spikes of 80ms per prefetch
```

lee: prefetch worker causing extra CPU work + IO maybe blocking main thread? we had prefetch designed to be async but recent change wired it sync on canary for easier debugging.

sam: oh — true, the canary flip accidentally set prefetch_sync=true via a config mismatch in deploy manifest. that would add latency on first token generation.

maya: canary-only sync prefetch + bigger microbatches = cocktail for tail. need to rollback prefetch first and then density. bisect plan?

dmitri: propose: 1) flip prefetch_sync -> false on canary 2) monitor p99 3) if still high, revert density param to 0.6 4) if still high rollback canary. can we patch canary fast?

ci-bot: Patch request created: PR #1124 to set prefetch_sync=false for canary.

sam: applying PR to canary now. rolling patch id p-452 -> canary hosts updated.

oncall-bot: Alert: p99 spike detected on canary. threshold breached at 1847200023.

lee: any early signal after patch?

sam: metrics after patch (2m): p99 dropped from 420ms -> 150ms on canary; p95 -> 130ms. still slightly above baseline p95 but p99 almost back.

maya: ok that points to prefetch_sync as main culprit. we should revert density change too to be safe before promoting.

dmitri: I pushed rollback of density to 0.6 on canary (config patch p-453). canary now matches baseline density.

ci-bot: Canary config updated: density=0.6.

sam: final check: p50=43ms, p95=125ms, p99=135ms on canary — within acceptable SLO. moving to full rollback of deploy d-78c2 (we won't promote).

sam: we aborted promotion and rolled back deploy d-78c2 across all hosts. marking incident resolved. :white_check_mark:

lee: please add a QA checklist: ensure prefetch flag default is async and that canary manifests don't flip to sync by default. also add unit to catch density>0.8 in canary configs.

maya: filing follow-up ticket for kernel-selector tests + add a perf unit test for prefetch sync behavior.

sam: thanks everyone. postmortem please include timeline and the config diff that introduced prefetch_sync.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved at 1847200175.
